WHO publishes second edition of the Global Code of Practice on the International Recruitment of Health Personnel
articles.description: WHO has published the second edition of the Global Code of Practice on the International Recruitment of Health Personnel, bringing together in a single document the Code adopted by the World Health Assembly in 2010 and the amendments adopted in May 2026. The new edition provides Member States and partners with an updated framework for managing the growing international mobility of health workers in ways that support stronger and more sustainable health systems. It reflects the increasing importance of international recruitment in responding to health workforce needs, while recognizing that its benefits and costs are not always equitably shared. At the heart of the updated Code is a shift towards co-investment and proportional benefits. International recruitment should increasingly be accompanied by arrangements where source and destination countries, together with development partners where appropriate, jointly invest in health workforce and health system priorities identified by source countries, including health workforce education, employment, retention and broader system strengthening. This approach seeks to ensure that the benefits generated by health worker mobility are shared more fairly among migrant health workers, source countries and destination countries. “Co-investment is not about placing a price on individual health workers or restricting their right to migrate,” explained Dr Tomas Zapata, Director of the WHO Academy. “Rather, it aims to move international recruitment towards mutually beneficial partnerships that expand professional and economic opportunities for health workers while strengthening health systems, including in countries experiencing workforce shortages.” The second edition incorporates the first amendments to the Code since its adoption 16 years ago. These provide greater clarity on its application during emergencies and to health workers employed as care workers in destination countries, while substantially strengthening the emphasis on co-investment. The amendments followed the third review of the Code by a Member State-led Expert Advisory Group, which reaffirmed its growing relevance and identified areas requiring stronger implementation. WHO will continue to support Member States, upon request, in implementing the updated Code, including through technical assistance on bilateral agreements, co-investment approaches and policy dialogue. “The Code remains a distinctive international instrument dedicated specifically to health workforce migration. Through its stronger focus on co-investment, shared responsibility and proportional benefits, the second edition provides a renewed framework for turning international health worker mobility into a driver of stronger health systems and shared prosperity,” said Dr Zapata. WHO Global Code of Practice on the International Recruitment of Health Personnel, 2nd ed.
